problems: 'more than a tool' can read as 'in addition to being a tool' or 'rather than a tool'
'mind' undefined
reviews.rewrite: AI is better understood as a new kind of mind than as a tool or artifact.

problems: 'real risk' has no threshold: anyone granting a non-zero chance can agree, so agreement is inflated
fixing it needs a stated magnitude, which would change the proposition
'inevitable' is a loaded word that casts the other side as fatalist
false dichotomy: choice vs inevitability
unclear if descriptive (is decided) or normative (should be)
reviews.rewrite: How technology reshapes work and society is set by collective choices rather than by a fixed course of development.

problems: 'without any change' is an absolute that makes the claim sound extreme and easy to reject
no time frame for 'better off'
reviews.rewrite: Technology-driven productivity growth makes most workers better off even if public policy stays as it is.

problems: near-universal agreement; disagreeing sounds anti-freedom or anti-democratic, so it barely discriminates
'compatible' could mean always, usually or in principle
cannot be sharpened without changing the proposition
'hype' is a pejorative from one camp's vocabulary
'inflated hype' is redundant and doubles the loading
'public promises' by whom is unclear
reviews.rewrite: Most public claims about what advanced AI will achieve are overstated.

problems: 'humane' is a positive label that makes agreeing feel virtuous
bundles liberal and humane ideals, which some see as different
'inherent force' is vague
reviews.rewrite: Liberal and humane ideals are strong enough in themselves to win out in long contests between societies.

problems: 'limits' has no degree: almost everyone accepts that competition limits some harm, so critics may agree while meaning 'a little'
a fix needs a stated degree, which would change the meaning
'serves human beings' and 'the end' are loaded, so disagreeing sounds anti-human
second clause is a straw version of transhumanist views
two claims joined
reviews.rewrite: AI should exist for the sake of humans, rather than humans being a stage that AI or its successors should move beyond.

problems: 'inflated by hype' is loaded and redundant
'outruns what it has shown' sets the bar at demonstrated results, which forecasters reject by definition
near-duplicate of ai-promises-inflated
reviews.rewrite: Public discussion of AI claims more than the technology has so far demonstrated.

problems: 'present' vs 'autonomous superintelligent' frames one side as concrete and the other as speculative
false dichotomy
unclear where future human misuse falls
reviews.rewrite: Dangers from how people use AI today deserve more attention than dangers from future autonomous superintelligent AI.

problems: 'may come to' is a weak hedge that makes agreeing very easy
bundles 'rights' (strong) with 'moral consideration' (weaker)
splitting them would change the proposition
'valid' is an approving epistemic word
bundles how AI will behave with how it will be received
'behave' is vague for a technology
reviews.rewrite: The history of earlier general-purpose technologies is a good guide to how AI will behave and how people will receive it.

problems: bundles base rates with average informed opinion, which are different things
'deferring' slightly connotes submission while 'informed' connotes respectability; these roughly cancel out
reviews.rewrite: On hard questions, base rates or the average of informed opinion should by default outweigh one's own reasoning.

problems: 'remain' presupposes it is the basis now
'rule by ... unelected powers' is pejorative, making disagreement sound authoritarian
lumps experts with executives
reviews.rewrite: Political authority should rest on popular self-government rather than on experts, executives or other unelected bodies.

problems: 'serves human beings' is warm language that makes disagreement sound misanthropic
'on balance' hedges only the agree side
reviews.rewrite: On balance, market-driven technological development is good for people.

problems: 'binding rules' covers anything from disclosure to licensing, so agreers may mean very different things
'stringent' makes the regulation sound excessive and the harm claim easier to accept
bundles the verdict (more harm than good) with the mechanism (deterring innovation)
separating them would change the proposition
'remain' presupposes AI development is separate now
'separate from state' echoes church-state separation
unclear whether funding, contracts or regulation count as direction
reviews.rewrite: The state should not direct or control AI development.

problems: 'cooperation across diverse groups' is warm, consensus language
'convergence on a singularity' is jargon and a straw version of the other side
few people say they aim at a singularity
reviews.rewrite: Technology should aim to help diverse groups work together, rather than to bring about a technological singularity.

problems: 'protect its lead' presupposes the US leads
bundles pressing ahead with protecting a lead
reviews.rewrite: Rivalry with China is a sound reason for the United States to press ahead in advanced technology and stay ahead of China.

problems: bundles wealth (e.g. cash or UBI) with ownership (e.g. equity or funds), which camps judge differently
splitting them would change the proposition
'slowed or stopped' bundles a moderate and a strong position, so 'agree' mixes both
splitting them would change the proposition
bundles feasibility ('can') with desirability ('should')
'should ... lead to good outcomes' is close to a truism, pulling toward agree
a pessimist about feasibility has no clean answer; it cannot be split without changing the proposition
